llm.summary: The skill is mostly a legitimate Aliyun OSS deployment helper, but it includes high-impact cloud publishing and automatically reuses local GitHub credentials in ways users should review carefully.

dimensions.detail: The OSS workflow deliberately disables bucket public-access blocking and publishes objects anonymously, which fits a public static site but needs tighter safeguards to avoid exposing the wrong bucket or mixed private content.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is conventional skill placement or git clone; I found no install-time hooks, obfuscated bootstrap, or remote code execution beyond normal dependency installation guidance.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions and set_github_secret.py can extract a token from ~/.git-credentials and use it for GitHub API operations, including writing Actions secrets and variables, without a strong explicit confirmation step.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Certificate material and state are stored under ~/.acme-oss and renewal is intended to run on a schedule; this is disclosed and purpose-aligned, but it creates persistent credentials and cloud mutation authority.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The package coherently supports static-site deployment to Aliyun OSS, public hosting, domain/certificate operations, GitHub Actions secrets/variables, and deployment verification.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intend to let an agent modify Aliyun OSS/DNS/certificate settings and GitHub Actions configuration. Use a dedicated public OSS bucket, least-privilege Aliyun RAM credentials, and an explicitly provided fine-scoped GitHub token; avoid relying on automatic ~/.git-credentials fallback. Review any operation that disables public-access blocking, writes repository secrets, or schedules certificate renewal before running it.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Downgraded: individual helper scripts only cover parts of the workflow, but the package as a whole includes OSS deployment, certificate/domain handling, GitHub secret management, and verification, so the advertised purpose is broadly supported.
[PE3] unexpected: Accepted as a material concern for ~/.git-credentials: GitHub authentication is relevant, but automatic local credential-store parsing is overbroad and under-controlled for a skill that can modify repository Actions secrets and variables.
[SQP-2] expected: Partly accepted: disabling OSS BlockPublicAccess is expected for a public static website, but the artifact does not strongly require a dedicated public bucket or an explicit wrong-bucket safety check.
[SC2] expected: Overridden: the cited curl usage is for verification and GitHub API calls, not downloading and executing remote scripts.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Partly accepted: triggers such as generic deployment or上线 wording are broad for a high-impact cloud deployment workflow and could route the skill when the user has not clearly opted into OSS static-site publishing.
[AS3] expected: Overridden: the README shows the intended install path for this skill's own files and does not instruct the agent to enumerate or read other installed skills.
[LP3] unexpected: Accepted as contextual concern: the skill uses shell, filesystem, network, cloud APIs, and credentials, but the manifest does not define explicit permission boundaries or confirmation requirements.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: Chinese-language instructions match the artifact's audience and do not create an independent security concern.
[E1] expected: Downgraded: calls to api.github.com are expected for listing and writing GitHub Actions secrets/variables; the concern is credential scope and confirmation, not unrelated exfiltration.
